title: Rabbi Huna Rova of Tzippori
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: He was Rabbi Yochanan’s student, as in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, end of chapter 4: “Rabbi Huna Rova (and in Rosh Hashanah, end of chapter 4, Rabbi Chunah Rabbah) of Tzippori in the name of Rabbi Yochanan”; and so it is in Taanit 4:2. In Shekalim 1:1: “Rabbi Chunah Rabbah of Tzippori (in Gittin 4:9, Rabbi Huna of Tzippori) said: Rabbi Chanina instituted in Tzippori,” etc.; and so it is in Demai 5:8. In Rosh Hashanah 34b, “Rav Huna of Tzippori said that Rabbi Yochanan said,” according to Dikdukei Soferim’s reading; the Gemara reads Rabbi Chanah. In Chullin 51a Rav Safra said to Abaye: “Let the Master see this Torah scholar who came from the West” … Abaye went to him … he said to him: “I was an attendant of assemblies, [standing] above Rabbi Rabbah (Rashi explains: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi; the author of Yuchasin already objected to this identification; Hyman considers Rabbi Yehudah Nesia undoubtedly the intended reading; Yuchasin HaShalem says that he means Rabbi Yochanan, who was called ‘Rabbi Rabbah’), and Rav Huna of Tzippori and Rabbi Yose of Mera’ah were sitting before him,” etc.

He is likewise mentioned at the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Taanit, chapter 2; Tanchuma, Va’era 9 and Shemini 10; and Pesikta deRav Kahana, historical locator 124:, as Rabbi Chunah Rabbah of Tzippori. Of those who speak in his name we find, in Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:2, Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha; and in Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 2:2, Rabbi Acha bar Yitzchak in the name of Rabbi Chunah Rova of Tzippori.
In Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 1:1: Rabbi Yudah ben Pazi and Rabbi Chanin in the name of Rabbi Chunah Rova of Tzippori. In Yoma 77b: Rabbi Pinchas in the name of Rav Huna of Tzippori.
He is mentioned in Bereshit Rabbah 8:5 as Rabbi Huna, the great one of Tzippori.

notes.text: מפטיר כנסיות is an assembly attendant, not someone who dismisses assemblies. Saved Davidson Chullin51a paragraphs3–4 has RavAvira recounting his position standing above Rabbi, with RavHuna and Yose seated below; the spatial above is retained, not rank. Rashi’s RabbiYehudahHaNasi and Hyman/Yuchasin’s alternative YehudahNesia or Yochanan identifications remain separate attributed readings. Historical Pesikta124: has no unproved page/column identity.

The consulted Chullin 51a 3–4 has Rav Safra speaking to Abaye about Rav Avira, followed by the attendant’s account. Its standing above is spatial, not rank. Directly consulted Rashi explains the role as gathering and dismissing students and identifies Rabbi Rabbah as Yehudah HaNasi. This comparison supplements, without rewriting, the retained current note’s narrower attendant wording. Hyman’s undoubtedly Nesia reading and the reported Yuchasin Yochanan alternative remain separately attributed; historical Pesikta 124: pagination is unbound.
